title: Christmas Proclamation (The Proclamation of the Birth of Christ)
notes:
The Christmas Proclamation, also known as the Proclamation of the Birth of Christ, is a solemn proclamation traditionally chanted or recited before the celebration of Midnight Mass on Christmas Eve, or on Christmas morning. It places the birth of Christ within the context of salvation history, referencing key events and figures from the Old Testament and ancient history.

The proclamation announces the birth of Jesus Christ in relationship to all of salvation history—from creation, through the flood, Abraham, Moses, David, to the fullness of time when 'the whole world being at peace.' This poetic and solemn proclamation helps us understand that Christ's birth is the center and fulfillment of all history.

The numbers used in the proclamation are based on the calculations found in the Roman Martyrology. While the exact dates may differ from modern historical scholarship, the proclamation serves a liturgical and spiritual purpose: to situate Christ's birth at the center of human history and as the fulfillment of God's plan of salvation.
description: The solemn proclamation of the birth of Christ from the Roman Martyrology, traditionally proclaimed at Christmas Midnight Mass
